steps.cap: Specks of dust and tiny flaws land at random on every wafer. A textbook example assumes 0.8 per square centimeter.
Of chips 1 centimeter on a side, 49.2 percent miss every speck and come out flawless.
Chips 2 centimeters on a side are bigger targets for the same specks. Only 11.3 percent come out flawless.
The big chip yields less and fits fewer times on a wafer, so it costs 20.1 times as much as the small one.
